title: A $10 WoW Panda Pet Raised $1.1 Million for Make-A-Wish
hook: In November 2009 Blizzard sold a $10 panda pet in World of Warcraft and gave half of every sale to Make-A-Wish. Three months later it handed over a check for $1.1 million. Which WoW pet would you pay ten bucks for?
script: Did you know a ten dollar virtual panda in World of Warcraft raised more than a million dollars for charity? On November fourth, two thousand nine, Blizzard surprised players by opening a Pet Store for the game. It was the first time Blizzard had sold in game items for real money in WoW. There were just two pets at launch. One was a tiny lich who shoots ice and has a diabolical laugh. The other was the Pandaren Monk, a little panda who bows back when you bow to him. Each cost ten dollars, and both were purely cosmetic. Blizzard promised that half of every Pandaren Monk sale through the end of the year would go to the Make-A-Wish Foundation. One week after launch, the store briefly listed the Monk as sold out. Blizzard blamed a minor technical error and put it back on sale. The following February, Blizzard handed Make-A-Wish a check worth more than a million dollars. Fifteen wish children and their families were invited to the ceremony at Blizzard's headquarters in Irvine. The next year a baby moonkin pet did it again, raising hundreds of thousands more for Make-A-Wish. Not bad for a panda that follows you around Azeroth. So which WoW pet would you pay ten dollars for?
